definition: A nociceptor is a pain-related sensory nerve fiber that can be activated when depolarization reaches a high enough level to trigger action potentials. In this source, nociceptors are described as C-fibers, including heat- and mechanosensitive polymodal fibers.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define a nociceptor as a “pain-related sensory nerve fiber.” It uses the term “nociceptors” and discusses relevance to pain clinically, but it does not provide that definitional phrasing.

The definition’s claim that a nociceptor “can be activated when depolarization reaches a high enough level to trigger action potentials” is not stated as a general definition in the packet. The packet discusses VGSC NaV1.7 facilitating action potential generation upon slow depolarization, but it does not describe this as the defining activation threshold for nociceptors.

The parts of the definition about nociceptors being C-fibers and including heat- and mechanosensitive polymodal fibers are consistent with the packet, but the above unsupported definitional elements prevent a full pass.
The packet supports a study of pig C-HT nociceptors/C-fibers, but it does not establish as a general source definition that nociceptors are pain-related sensory nerve fibers.
The packet does not support the broad claim that nociceptors, as such, are C-fibers; it only mentions heat-mechanosensitive polymodal nociceptors (C-HT) in this study.
